extracted.intended_audience: telecom industry stakeholders, INCOMPAS members, policymakers, FCC staff, and congressional staff
extracted.subtask_description: A set of organizational policy positions and recommended regulatory changes across broadband deployment, Universal Service Fund reform, AI policy, spectrum use, and voice/messaging intended to guide advocacy and regulatory comments in 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote competitive broadband alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocating for federal, state, and local policies that enable competitive broadband alternatives in every community, which will lead to more innovation, investment, and affordability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on policies that lower barriers to entry and support multiple providers competing in local markets; emphasize benefits such as innovation, investment, and affordability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support deployment of robust, scalable fiber/gigabit infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting the deployment of robust, scalable, competitive broadband network capability throughout the U.S., including fiber-based, gigabit and above infrastructure that will provide a connectivity foundation for 5G and future generation networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize policies and programs that facilitate investment in fiber and high-capacity networks as the backbone for mobile and future services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure competitive providers are included in BEAD implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Track BEAD implementation and ensure that competitive providers that are best positioned to serve local communities are part of the solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for BEAD/other grant processes and rules that do not unfairly exclude competitive providers; monitor implementation details to protect competitive participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support state and local policies enabling wholesale access
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting state and local policies that will enable more broadband competition through reasonable wholesale access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote reasonable wholesale access regimes at state and local levels to facilitate competition and last-mile alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitting and pole attachment reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocating the FCC for permitting and pole attachment reform (including make-ready timelines for large pole attachment projects and clarifying that new attachers are not solely responsible for pole replacement costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Push for clear make-ready timelines and cost-allocation rules so pole attachment processes are predictable and do not unduly burden new entrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal access to residential and commercial multiple-tenant environments (MTEs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing competitive providers with equal access to residential and commercial multiple tenant environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek rules or enforcement that prevent landlord or incumbent practices from blocking competitive access to MTEs; emphasize fair access for competitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stabilize the high USF contribution factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocating the FCC to stabilize the high contribution factor, which telecom customers ultimately pay as an additional fee on their monthly telecom bills in order to finance the USF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek measures to reduce volatility and burden of the contribution factor on consumers and providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Put USF on a sustainable path (appropriations or expand base to BIAS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocating to Congress’ bipartisan, bicameral USF Working Group to put the USF on a sustainable path forward through appropriations or by expanding the base to include BIAS revenues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support legislative or policy changes that make USF funding sustainable, including expanding the revenue base beyond traditional telecom services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propose reasonable changes to USF distributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed reasonable changes to USF distributions, including the High-Cost program, that would phase out some support mechanisms that are no longer needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate targeted reforms to distribution programs to reflect current deployment realities and avoid wasteful subsidies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find USF savings by considering IIJA broadband funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocate that the FCC consider the billions of dollars that Congress has provided through the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act for broadband deployment and affordability and find savings in the USF programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage coordination between federal grant funding and USF program design to avoid duplicated spending and identify offsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote open networks, open markets, and competition in technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Promoting open networks, open markets, and competition in telecommunications and technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate policies that preserve openness and competition across platforms and services to spur innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve competition across the entire technology stack
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocating the founding principle of competition to ensure a robust ecosystem to promote competition and innovation throughout the entire technology stack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy positions should consider competition at infrastructure, platform, and application layers to prevent concentration and anticompetitive lock-in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with AI Competition Center and use a national AI framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Work in consultation with the INCOMPAS-affiliated Artificial Intelligence Competition Center, which has developed a national framework for harnessing the transformational power of AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align organizational AI policy advocacy with the Competition Center's framework; use that framework when drafting comments and proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare workforce and support comprehensive retraining programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare the future workforce and support comprehensive retraining programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Push for policies and programs that fund training and retraining to help workers transition as technologies change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pair robust fiber networks with abundant data center capacity in energy strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Drive a comprehensive “all-of-the-above” energy strategy that pairs robust fiber networks with abundant data center capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate integrated strategies that consider energy, fiber, and data center planning to support digital infrastructure growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish clear protocols for AI in national security while protecting civil liberties
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish clear protocols for AI use in national security applications while protecting civil liberties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support policy that enables legitimate national security uses of AI but includes safeguards for privacy and civil liberties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enact federal privacy legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: Enact federal privacy legislation to provide consistent consumer protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for baseline federal privacy rules to replace fragmented state regimes and provide consistent protections for consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase competition using mid-band and millimeter wave spectrum
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting efforts to increase competition for broadband through the broader use of mid-band and millimeter wave spectrum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote policies that open additional mid-band and mmWave spectrum to support diverse broadband use cases and providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstate FCC auction authority and empower FCC to leverage spectrum
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocating Congress to reinstate the FCC’s auction authority and empower the FCC to leverage the nation’s spectrum resources for more licensed and unlicensed broadband use cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support statutory changes that give the FCC flexible tools (including auctions) to allocate spectrum for competitive outcomes and a mix of licensed/unlicensed use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modernize 12.2-12.7 GHz rules for high-powered two-way fixed broadband
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocate the FCC to take immediate action in the 12.2-12.7 GHz proceeding to modernize its rules to permit high-powered, two-way fixed broadband service in the band.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Push for rule changes that allow new two-way fixed broadband deployments in that band to increase broadband options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finalize technology-neutral licensed sharing in 37.0-37.6 GHz
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocate the FCC to finalize a technology-neutral, licensed sharing framework in the 37.0-37.6 GHz band so the spectrum can be made available for increased commercial use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote frameworks that are technology-neutral and allow sharing to maximize commercial use and competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fill regulatory gaps for wholesale providers and enterprise customers
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocating for solutions that will fill current regulatory gaps (including gaps for wholesale providers and enterprise customers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify areas where existing regulation does not address wholesale or enterprise scenarios and propose tailored rules or clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary restrictions and tailor rules for smaller competitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid putting any unnecessary restrictions that impact the ability of voice providers to innovate and compete, and are tailored appropriately for smaller competitors based on their resource constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate proportionate regulation that does not impose undue burdens on smaller or resource-constrained competitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance IP transition and STIR/SHAKEN across IP-interconnected networks
rubrics_metrics.description: To mitigate fraudulent robocalling and robotexting activity, advocate that the Commission must advance the IP transition to ensure STIR/SHAKEN operates across IP-interconnected networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support policies and timelines that accelerate IP transition and ensure authentication frameworks like STIR/SHAKEN work end-to-end across networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve provider flexibility to incorporate AI in robocall mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve the flexibility that providers have to incorporate AI technologies into their mitigation efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppose rules that would rigidly prohibit use of AI tools for mitigation; allow innovation in detection and blocking methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute robust call/text blocking notification and redress mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Institute robust call/text blocking notification and redress mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require transparent notification to consumers about blocking and accessible remedies/redress for mistaken blocking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure anti-robocall efforts do not discriminate against competitive providers
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure industry efforts to manage or label illegal robocalls do not intentionally or inadvertently discriminate against competitive providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate safeguards and oversight to prevent discriminatory implementation of labeling/blocking systems that disadvantage competitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocate sensible solutions for copper retirement and IP transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocate for sensible solutions that address major providers’ attempts to retire copper infrastructure and transition to IP-based technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support transition plans that protect consumers and competition when incumbents retire legacy copper networks and move to IP.
